The Juniors have performed with great credit, and tribute must be paid to the excellent running of Derrick Burfitt. Still in his middle 'teens he has a formidable series of wins to his name.
It will be interesting to see how Derrick Burfitt acquits himself on the track at whatever distance he decides to try after his very successful season on the country.
A large field turned out for an annual …amiliar faces, including many of our "Service" members who came along for the race. The winner proved to be D.
Derrick Burfitt, John Brown and Ken Cuff kept together until about half-way, when Burfitt gradually went away to win a good race from John Brown.

In the One Mile, Derrick Burfitt produced a burst of speed at the finish which nobody could match to win in 4 mins. 39 secs. His nearest rival, Chard (T.V.H.), had previously beaten him by a very narrow margin in the corresponding Middlesex County event.
Derrick Burfitt has to attend week-end classes so we won't be seeing much of him this winter. He intends to keep fit, however, under the watchful eye of Fred Ford.

The past winter has shown us that we can still lead the way and we congratulate our runners and walkers on a good season's work. Once again Derrick Burfitt has merited special mention. He won the National Youth's Cross-Country Race by a convincing margin.

This was held over the same course and on the same day as the Senior Race, and Derrick Burfitt, who a week ago had won the County Youths' Championship (3½ miles), won in 32.43—two seconds faster than the winner (M.

Derrick Burfitt won as he liked in the Youths' One Mile in 4.30. Fred Clay, feeling the effects of a strenuous afternoon the previous Saturday at Dartford, lost his heat in the 100, but won his 220 yards first heat in 24.4, but failed to qualify in the second round.

Derrick Burfitt has again been in a class of his own, winning all of his races with the grand ease of a champion. The best team effort was undoubtedly the gaining of third place in the English Youth's event, held at Leamington Spa on the same day as the "National ." Our lads have done well in the va…
Derrick Burfitt, our junior champion, was an easy winner of the individual race, and he was followed home by two more club members, in Dave Main 2, and Geoff.

Derrick Burfitt, our "National" youth champion, once again proved his outstanding ability by running away from his field, and he clocked 30 mins. for our usual 5 miles course, which is very good running.
Geoff Pearson and Dave Main ran well to come in together for 3rd place in the individual race, and Dick Tobin was 6th. Derrick Burfitt retained his Middlesex Junior Title.

Under Alf's guidance the juniors rapidly became a fighting force in team events and led by Derrick Burfitt, who has rightly been described as the best junior runner in the country, they did very well in open events.
Coming to the Junior Championships, we find, once again, the name of Derrick Burfitt at the head in the 1 Mile, he won both National and Southern titles.
Derrick Burfitt, was, of course, outstanding in his performances, and we look forward to a continuation of his successes, both on track and country.
At the British Games meeting held at the White City, Derrick Burfitt won the 880 yards Youths' Race, while Basil Walden was third in the final of the 100 yards Youths' Scratch Race.
In the 1 Mile Medley Relay, it was unfortunate that after Derrick Burfitt, running a 2 min. 1 sec. half mile, had given us a good lead that we had to run Len Bishop over the final 440 yards stage.
Derrick Burfitt turned out for the Club in the 1 Mile team race and won easily. With Eddie Short second and Len Bishop third, we won the team race with the lowest possible score.

Eric Bishop gained third place in the 880, and then in the 1 Mile we called upon Derrick Burfitt to assist us, and he simply walked away from his field, and Derrick certainly makes running look a very easy business.

Stan Botwright won the 440 and beat both Pettet and Moody, who were running for the Police in this event. Derrick Burfitt, on his home track, turned out for us in the 1 Mile and won easily in 4 min. 32.3 secs.

In the 1 Mile we had expected Derrick Burfitt to make a bold challenge to Len Herbert, the holder, but Derrick decided to save himself for the Bank Holiday meeting at the White City, where he was running for the English A.T.C. against the French Juniors.
The Track and Field Events Sections had also performed well. The Juniors had maintained very good progress, with Derrick Burfitt again pre-eminent.

Len Herbert ran a magnificent race to win the Senior race, and Derrick Burfitt found a fine finish to win the Junior race. A weakened team in the Seniors were second to Aylesford Paper Mills and the Junior team ran very well to finish third to S.L.H. and T.V.H.
Harley (Senior), Etienne Gailly, George Durrant, Derrick Burfitt, Norman Graves and the Wirral A.C. (with a Wirral whisper!), Dick Towndrow, Mr. and Mrs.
Michael Broadbent and Derrick Burfitt have been mentioned in the press as being British Olympic hopes. We believe they can do it given the chances, and we hope others will join them by 1948.
We had the first three men home in Derrick Burfitt, Eddie Short and Arthur Bruce, who came in together, and they were followed by Len Bishop.
Finchley had the first two men home and then came Derrick Burfitt, who made light of the conditions, although losing a shoe, and having to catch up on his field again.

In the 2 Miles Run, Derrick Burfitt, the A.A.A. junior mile champion, was on the virtual scratch mark of 20 yards. He ran an excellent race to work his way through the field, and although Vic Blowfield hung closely on his heels, Derrick finished a good second to Len Marchant, the winner, with a yard…
Derrick Burfitt retained his hold on the Junior title, which he won in 34 mins. 18 secs., and this makes his fourth successive win, which must be a record which will last for all time.
However, we do thank him for turning out at short notice and we were also pleased to see Derrick Burfitt present although he only arrived home on leave that same morning.
Len Herbert, the holder, ran a splendid race to retain his title in 4 min. 24.4 secs., and Bill Lucas just beat Derrick Burfitt for second place.

Derrick Burfitt retained his title but only after a hard fight with young Robertson of Reading, who made his effort too soon, although we must confess the finishing post was not clear owing to spectators encroaching on the course.

Derrick Burfitt found his R.A.F. duties against record-breaking performances, which has been his wont in the past, but even so he turned out for the club whenever he was home on leave and we much appreciated his help.
Vic Blowfield and Derrick Burfitt also picked up useful points in the 1 mile event, and our team also won the team race in the 2 miles race.

The holder of the title, Derrick Burfitt, was a non-runner as Derrick is not doing anything over the country this season in view of the coming Olympic Games, in which he is on the list of "possibles." A very close and interesting race was seen between Eddie Short, Martin Williamson and Arthur Bruce.

The final was a grand race between the three heat winners, and in a "blanket" finish Alan Sexton was adjudged the winner with Les Christmas second and George Lowers third. The field for the two miles run was more numerous, although both Len Herbert and Derrick Burfitt were non-starters.
This lad looks a second Derrick Burfitt, having much the same style, and he won the Surrey County Youths 1 mile title in fine style.
The South of Thames Championship was won, despite barring clauses, for the third time in four years, with Derrick Burfitt leading the field home.
Derrick Burfitt, won the R.A.F.
Frank Abberton was the individual winner of the Surrey race and Derrick Burfitt only failed by a couple of yards to repeat this performance in the Middlesex event.

Over the first small lap Peter Curry, the Olympic Games steeplechase representative was in the lead closely followed by Derrick Burfitt. On completion of the first big lap, Curry and Burfitt had drawn away from the rest of the field and were running stride for stride.
We were pleased to see Derrick Burfitt out again, and he led the field from start to finish, with Archie Bedford as runner-up and George Lucas third.

A good field was seen in the 2 miles run and Eric Bishop, off 260 yds., was a good winner with Martin Williamson, off 180, second, and Lou Bush, off 300 yds., third. Derrick Burfitt ran well, off a back mark, to run through to sixth position, and looks to be in for a good season over the country.
Starting from Mitcham, our runner on the first stage to Purley was Derrick Burfitt. He did well to finish 5th in 30 mins. 6 secs.
Derrick Burfitt did best for the club by gaining third place in the mile and as this race was won in the fast time of 4 mins. 15 secs., he can be said to have done very well.
Derrick Burfitt only just lost a fast half in 1 min. 59 secs., Len Marchant won the mile in 4 mins. 29 secs., and Len Herbert the 2 miles in 9 mins. 47 secs.
In the 880 yards John Cope was fifth in his heat. In the mile, Derrick Burfitt won his heat in 4.20, but in the final was seventh in 4 min. 19 secs.
Derrick Burfitt was content to take things easy and came in with George Still who completed the course in good style and is really a wonder for his age.

Derrick Burfitt then took over and set about the opposition in his usual determined fashion and he eventually handed over to Jack Brown in second place with the Aylesford runner the only one he had failed to overtake.

The course was a sticky one of 7½ miles and Derrick Burfitt was first man home followed by Ted Stimpson. Vern Blowfield had an easy run in fourth position and it looks as if these three will form the spearhead of our team for the coming cross-country championships.
At the end of the first lap Vern Blowfield and Derrick Burfitt were running stride for stride in the lead followed by Les Stokell and Jack Brown.
In the recent Civil Service cross-country championship, Derrick Burfitt was placed 3rd, with Eric Herbert 7th, Jack Brown 9th and Rene Howell 11th.
Derrick Burfitt was second in this race last year, but this time could not get nearer than eighth with Vern Blowfield ninth. As the first seven home included such runners as Alec Olney, D.

Len Herbert was also a non-starter and on the first lap Derrick Burfitt developed a blistered heel and so wisely withdrew. At the half-distance there was a group of four runners with Brown, Blowfield, Bill Lucas and Steve Charlton all nicely together in under the half-hour, which is good running for…

To try to find the reason for our dropping off is partly explained when we find runners like Len Herbert, Derrick Burfitt, Bill Lucas, Frank Abberton, Reg Ruddick and Eddie Short not taking part in the big races and although we are a club of considerable numerical strength, it takes time to build up…
Mick Porter and Mike Stearman followed by Len Adams also did well but Derrick Burfitt was suffering from a heavy cold and never seemed to get really going.
… can say is that Vern Blowfield was not disgraced in handing over in 9th position and his time was actually faster than Derrick Burfitt did over the same leg last year.…

In the 1 mile, Derrick Burfitt and Jack Brown strode round in the lead and never looked like being troubled and they ran in together. We scored major points in three of the five field events with our Latvian member, A.

We scored our only win of the meeting in the 1 Mile with Derrick Burfitt beating Morley of Southgate in quite good time, and as the latter had beaten Derrick the previous Wednesday when running for the A.A.A. against London University, this win gave our runner the chance to turn the tables on his opponent.

Vern Blowfield did 4.31, running first, then Jack Brown 4.34, Bill Lucas 4.46, and Derrick Burfitt 4.34 to come home winners. In the 3 miles Team Race we had Jack Bragginton, George Lucas, Steve Charlton and Len Bishop, but could only manage a 4th place in this event.

In the Middlesex Championships, Derrick Burfitt won the 1 mile in the fast time of 4 mins. 23.4 secs., while in the Hants Championships we are pleased to see our old friend, Percy Wright, still to the fore, when winning the 2 miles walk title.
The 1,000 yards saw our real strength and here we had the first three home in Derrick Burfitt, Ches Walker and Vernon Blowfield, with Jimmy Wood, of the Poly, 4th.

The heats of the 1 mile saw Jack Brown and Ches Walker competing and a notable absentee was Derrick Burfitt. Brown ran quite well to finish inside the standard time of 4 min. 25 secs., and Walker also gained standard and actually finished a very close fourth in his heat with the first three only goi…

Derrick Burfitt and Ches Walker were first and second in the 880 yards, and Bill Lucas won the 1 mile with Vern Blowfield in third place. Len Herbert won the 2 miles race in 9 min. 34.4 secs., but we were beaten in the team race by S.L.H.
Derrick Burfitt was not defending his 1 mile Senior title and Jack Brown ran a good race to beat Len Herbert with Bob Taylor gaining his first club championship medal in third place.
We thus led throughout and with Len Herbert, Derrick Burfitt, Vern Blowfield and Jack Brown to call on, it is a pity that the “ National ” Brighton Relay has been put off until April, 1951.
Goode, who is just turned 16 and bearing in mind that Derrick Burfitt won this race when about the same age, we hope that Goode will prove to be as good a runner as Derrick turned out to be.

Derrick Burfitt, the holder, Vernon Blowfield, who won in 1947, and Tom Carter, who scored wins in 1938, 1939 and then again when the race was resumed in 1945, were all absentees on this occasion, but even so, the field included two British Olympic representatives in Bill Lucas and Jack Braughton.
In the Middlesex events “Ginger” Holtum ran really well to finish second in the 100 yards, and our old member, Derrick Burfitt, won the 1 mile.

So to the final with two Australians in the field, also our old friends Derrick Burfitt and Doug Wilson, the "daddy of them all." It was an interesting race to watch and once again Bill Nankeville proved himself a master tactician by beating his opponents in the fast time of 4 min. 9.8 secs.

The past winter has shown us that we can still lead the way and we congratulate our runners and walkers on a good season's work. Once again Derrick Burfitt has merited special mention. He won the National Youth's Cross-Country Race by a convincing margin.
Starting from Mitcham, our runner on the first stage to Purley was Derrick Burfitt.
